title: Build a Simple CRUD API for Notes
description: Create a complete CRUD API for a Note resource using in‑memory storage.
problemStatement:
Implement a full CRUD API for managing `Note` objects. A note has:
- `id` (Long, automatically generated)
- `title` (String)
- `content` (String)

**Requirements:**
1. Create a `Note` class with fields, constructors, getters, and setters.
2. Create a `NoteService` that stores notes in an `ArrayList` (or `Map`) and provides methods: `findAll()`, `findById(id)`, `save(note)`, `update(id, note)`, `delete(id)`.
3. Create a `NoteController` with the following endpoints:
   - `GET /api/notes` – list all notes.
   - `GET /api/notes/{id}` – get a single note.
   - `POST /api/notes` – create a new note (return 201 Created).
   - `PUT /api/notes/{id}` – update an existing note.
   - `DELETE /api/notes/{id}` – delete a note (return 204 No Content).

**Bonus:** Add a `@PatchMapping` endpoint to partially update a note (e.g., only update the title or content).
hints: In the service, use a `List<Note>` and a counter for IDs.
In `update`, first find the existing note by ID, then modify its fields.
For the `save` method, assign a new ID before adding to the list.
Use `ResponseEntity` or `@ResponseStatus` to set the correct status codes.
expectedOutput:
The API should behave as described, returning JSON representations of notes. For example:

`GET /api/notes/1` → `{"id":1,"title":"First Note","content":"Hello world"}`

`POST /api/notes` with body `{"title":"New","content":"Content"}` → 201 Created, and returns the created note with an ID.
